sections.title: Governance & Accountability
sections.tagline: Without clear ownership, nothing else sticks.

questions.text: Has your organisation formally appointed someone responsible for data protection compliance, a Data Protection Officer, Privacy Officer, or equivalent?
Is there a Grievance Officer whose name, email, and postal address are publicly visible on your website or app?
Does a senior executive or board member hold accountability for your data protection programme, with authority to allocate budget and resolve cross-functional blockers?
Are roles and responsibilities for DPDP compliance clearly defined across Legal, IT, Security, Product, HR, and Marketing, with named owners for each obligation?
Has dedicated budget been allocated for data protection activities (tooling, training, legal counsel, external advisors)?

sections.title: Data Discovery & Inventory
sections.tagline: You can't protect what you don't know you have.

questions.text: Do you have a complete, up-to-date inventory of every category of personal data your organisation collects, processes, and stores?
Have you mapped how personal data flows through your systems, from initial collection, through every system it touches, to final deletion, including third-party processors?
Have you classified your data into tiers (e.g., sensitive, personal, pseudonymised) and tied controls and retention rules to each tier?
Do you maintain a record of the purpose and legal basis for every category of personal data you process?
Do you maintain a register of every vendor, partner, or third party that receives or accesses personal data on your behalf?

sections.title: Notice & Consent
sections.tagline: Every collection point needs a clean notice and, where required, valid consent.

questions.text: Do you display a clear, specific privacy notice at every point where you collect personal data, not buried in a general terms-and-conditions page?
Can you provide your privacy notice in any of the 22 scheduled Indian languages on request?
Do you collect consent separately for each distinct purpose (e.g., account creation, marketing emails, analytics), with no pre-ticked boxes and no bundling with Terms of Service?
Can a user withdraw their consent as easily as they gave it, for example, a single-click opt-out where a single click was used to opt in?
Do you maintain a tamper-evident audit trail of every consent event, recording who consented, to what, when, and which version of your notice was shown?
Have you reviewed your existing (legacy) user data to assess whether the consent obtained meets DPDP standards, and do you have a plan to re-consent where it does not?
Have you formally mapped each processing activity to either a consent basis or a specific DPDP "legitimate use", with no ambiguous or undocumented processing?
Is there a clearly signposted channel (web form, email, or in-app mechanism) where individuals can submit a request about their personal data, without needing to be logged in?
Can an individual receive a summary of the personal data your organisation holds about them, the purposes for which it is processed, and who it is shared with?
Can individuals request correction, completion, updating, or erasure of their personal data, and do you have a workflow that fulfils these requests end-to-end, including notifying processors?
Do you have defined, monitored SLAs for each type of rights request (access, correction, erasure, grievance)?
Can individuals nominate another person to exercise their data rights on their behalf in the event of death or incapacity?

sections.title: Children & Persons with Disabilities
sections.tagline: Extra obligations many teams overlook until audit.

questions.text: Do you have a mechanism to verify the age of users before collecting their data, beyond a self-declaration checkbox?
Where a user is under 18, do you obtain verifiable parental or guardian consent before processing their data?
Have you confirmed that children's accounts are excluded from behavioural tracking, targeted advertising, profiling, and recommendation models?

sections.title: Security Safeguards
sections.tagline: Reasonable security is a legal obligation, not just best practice.

questions.text: Is personal data encrypted in transit (TLS 1.2 or higher) and at rest (AES-256 or equivalent)?
Do employees have access only to the personal data they need for their specific role, and is this access reviewed regularly?
Is multi-factor authentication (MFA) mandatory for anyone with access to systems that contain personal data?
Do you run periodic vulnerability assessments or penetration tests on systems that hold personal data, and do you track remediation against defined SLAs?
Are your backups and disaster recovery plans for personal data systems documented, tested, and integrated with your data erasure workflow?

sections.title: Processor & Vendor Management
sections.tagline: Your liability does not end when the data leaves your environment.

questions.text: Do you have a signed Data Processing Agreement (DPA) with every vendor or partner that processes personal data on your behalf?
Do your vendor contracts require disclosure of sub-processors, flow-down of data protection obligations, and your prior approval for material changes?
Do your vendor contracts give you the right to audit or inspect how they handle your data (directly or via an independent third-party report)?
Do you conduct security and privacy due diligence (certifications, controls, sub-processors, prior breaches) before onboarding a new vendor?
Do you re-assess your vendors on a defined schedule, at least annually for high-volume or high-sensitivity processors?

sections.title: Personal Data Breach Management
sections.tagline: Speed and evidence are everything once something goes wrong.

questions.text: Do you have a written, tested incident response plan with a section specifically covering personal data breaches?
Are severity tiers, escalation paths, roles (Legal, DPO, Communications, Engineering), and communication templates pre-defined for a breach scenario?
Do you have a process to notify the Data Protection Board within the required statutory timeline, including a pre-drafted notification template and standing contact details?
Do you have a process to notify affected individuals in plain language, via the channels they normally use, with clear guidance on what they should do?
Do you maintain a breach register that records every incident (including near-misses), with root cause, impact, containment timeline, notification status, and lessons learned?

sections.title: Retention & Erasure
sections.tagline: The default is delete, keep only what you can justify.

questions.text: Do you have a documented retention schedule that specifies how long each category of personal data is kept and on what basis (legal, contractual, or business)?
Is data automatically deleted or anonymised when the retention period expires or the purpose for which it was collected is fulfilled?
Do you identify and erase the data of users who have not engaged with your service for a defined dormancy period, after notifying them?
When you terminate a vendor relationship or receive an erasure request, do you obtain written confirmation from the vendor that they have deleted the data (including backups and archives)?
Do you know every country where your personal data is transferred, stored, or remotely accessed, including via SaaS tools, analytics platforms, and support systems?
Do you actively monitor the Indian government's notified list of restricted countries for data transfers, and do you have a process to respond when it changes?
Do your contracts with overseas vendors include data protection safeguards, covering security measures, rights assistance, sub-processor controls, and cooperation with Indian regulators?

sections.title: Privacy by Design & Default
sections.tagline: Bake it in during build, not during audit.

questions.text: Is a privacy review built into your product development process, so new features are assessed for privacy risk before they are built and before they go live?
Are your product defaults set to the minimum data collection necessary, opt-in for marketing, analytics, and profiling rather than opt-out?

Do you conduct Data Protection Impact Assessments (DPIAs) for new, high-risk, or material changes to data processing, such as processing children's data, cross-border transfers, or automated decision-making?
Have all employees completed a DPDP awareness training module, and is completion tracked and attested?
Do teams with higher data-handling responsibilities, engineering, marketing, support, HR, sales, receive role-specific, deeper training on top of the baseline?
Is there an accessible internal channel where employees can ask privacy questions or report a data incident, and do they know it exists?

sections.title: Significant Data Fiduciary Obligations
sections.tagline: Plan for it early, even if you have not been notified yet.

questions.text: Has your organisation assessed whether it is likely to be classified as a Significant Data Fiduciary (SDF) based on data volume, sensitivity, or the nature of the business?
If classified as an SDF, are you prepared to appoint an India-resident, board-accountable Data Protection Officer (a full employee, not a consultant)?

Does your organisation use automated or algorithmic systems that make decisions affecting individuals (credit scoring, content moderation, eligibility, recommendations)? If yes, have you assessed the fairness, accuracy, and recourse implications?

sections.title: Documentation & Evidence
sections.tagline: If it is not written down and retrievable, it did not happen.

questions.text: Is your public-facing privacy policy current, written in plain language, and aligned with DPDP's specific disclosure requirements?
Do you maintain internal policies and SOPs for consent management, data rights requests, retention and erasure, breach response, and vendor management?
If a regulator, customer, or auditor asked you to produce evidence of compliance today, consent logs, rights request records, training completion, DPAs, could you do so within 24 hours?

sections.title: Monitoring & Continuous Improvement
sections.tagline: DPDP is a programme, not a one-time project.

questions.text: Do you have a compliance calendar that schedules recurring activities, audits, policy reviews, training refreshers, vendor reassessments, board reports?
Do you track and review compliance KPIs on a defined cadence, such as rights request SLA adherence, training completion rate, consent coverage, and percentage of vendors with signed DPAs?
Is there an owner responsible for monitoring new DPDP rules, Data Protection Board guidance, and Central Government notifications, and a process to update your programme in response?
